ledger.claim: Independently, POL-GEN-02(2) caps the confidence of any ruling that rests on the excess figure at the weight of the artifact carrying it - EV-GPS-00110 at 0.39. That is below the platform-wide floor of 0.70, so the case escalates automatically under POL-RD-10(1) even before the corroboration point is reached, and the ruling must name the artifact, its 0.39 weight and the codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

No route deviation is established on the governing figure, and the outcome is NO_ACTION. POL-RD-01 measures excess as trace distance less optimal distance: 21.2 km minus 18.4 km is 2.8 km, which is 15.2% of optimal, and the clause requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal and 0.8 km. The percentage gate fails, so the deviation is not established however the rider characterises the trip. The trace artifact is impaired (weight 0.39; issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE) and I rely on it with that impairment disclosed; the optimal figure comes from the trip record, which is clean.

The rider's own arithmetic does not reach the gate either. He pleads that the route 'is 18-19 km' against the 21.2 km charged, i.e. an excess of at most about 3 km on an 18.4 km optimal, roughly 16% - still short of POL-RD-01's 20% threshold. Taking the rider's case at its highest, both establishment tests cannot be met, so there is nothing to refund. The trace is impaired (weight 0.39; issues GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE) and is cited with that impairment disclosed.

No burden ever shifts to the driver.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-GPS-00110 at weight_multiplier 0.39 but does not name its issue code(s): GPS_GAP, LOW_COVERAGE

ledger.claim: The driver drove the platform's own optimal corridor, not a detour away from it. The trip record's routing engine (routing-engine-v3.2, LTA traffic snapshot 18:19) gives the optimal route as 'KPE then ECP, crossing both gantries' - the expressway the driver reports taking and the same corridor the rider's own claim names. A route that runs along the optimal corridor cannot deviate from it, and the residual 2.8 km is the ordinary ramp, merge and lane-change slack that POL-RD-01's single numeric gate exists to disregard.

The driver announced the route in the app before the vehicle reached the tunnel - 'going KPE ah boss' - and the rider answered 'ok'. The rider therefore knew the expressway route and raised no objection at the time; his statement that he 'was on my phone' explains why he did not watch the route, not why the route was wrong. The chat artifact is impaired (weight 0.6; issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, the export ending at 18:26:14) and I rely on it with that impairment disclosed; even discounting it, the exchange appears on the surviving page.

The $3.00 of ERP the rider disputes is properly chargeable. The trip record's optimal_route_erp_sgd is 3.00 and the platform's own optimal route crosses both gantries, so the toll sits on the optimal corridor the driver drove. The fare breakdown's erp_gantries is null, so under POL-RD-09(4) the gantry match is undecidable on the record, the line is treated as matched, and no billing-integrity refund arises - there is no phantom gantry here. The fare artifact is impaired (weight 0.75; issue code PARTIAL_RECORD) and is cited with that impairment disclosed.

Even if POL-RD-06 is consulted on a finely balanced record, no repeat-deviation pattern is established. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 744, so neither the three-flag test nor the 0.05 ratio test (with at least 40 completed trips) is met. No FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) can follow.

In the alternative, if the tunnel dropout is held to leave the excess genuinely unmeasurable, the only permissible route is ESCALATE, not a refund. POL-RD-07(ii)-(iii) require independent corroboration of any deviation and direct ESCALATE where none exists: the truncated chat contains no driver admission, erp_gantries is null, and trip_record.actual_distance_km is a copy of the impaired trace, so no POL-RD-07(ii) source is available. Under POL-RD-10(3) the disputed amount is then held rather than refunded while a human reviews it. Either way the driver is not required to return the fare.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-GPS-00110 at weight_multiplier 0.39 but does not name its issue code(s): GPS_GAP, LOW_COVERAGE

ledger.claim: The present payment state is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are, so on this rider-filed dispute a finding of no deviation means the fare stands and no money moves to the rider - the outcome the driver seeks. The fare artifact is impaired (weight 0.75; issue code PARTIAL_RECORD), disclosed here.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this case cannot be safely decided on the evidence, so it goes to a human reviewer. Here is why, in plain terms.

The only measurement of how far the vehicle actually travelled comes from the driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00110). That artifact is impaired. It contains a single 428-second dropout from 18:35:00 to 18:42:08, the fixes on either side of it are 6.9 km apart in a straight line, and the gap covers the whole KPE tunnel segment in dispute. A gap over 90 seconds engages POL-RD-07(a), so the trace is impaired for POLICY purposes, not merely by the admissibility pre-pass; both things are true and I say both. It carries weight 0.39 and the issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE, and the discount is applied throughout.

Measured the way POL-RD-07(i) directs - a straight line across the gap, the reading most favourable to the driver - the trip is 21.2 km against an optimal 18.4 km, an excess of 2.8 km or 15.2%, under POL-RD-01's 20% gate. The driver is right that on that reading no deviation is established. But that figure is a floor, not a measurement. The admissibility record for the same trace states that a surface route between the two bounding portals would put the trip at 25.5 km, which is over the gate. Nothing in the bundle distinguishes the two readings. So the excess can neither be established nor excluded: the limb is undecided, and under POL-RD-07(iii) that is a data failure, not a finding for the driver.

POL-RD-07(ii) permits a deviation on an impaired trace only with an independent source, and there is none. The chat (EV-CHAT-00110, weight 0.6, TRUNCATED_LOG) stops at 18:26:14, before the tunnel, and holds no admission - only the driver's 'going KPE ah boss' and the rider's 'ok'. The gantry itemisation on the fare (EV-FARE-00110, weight 0.75, PARTIAL_RECORD) is null, so the charged-gantry check cannot run. The 21.2 km on the trip record and the 21.2 km on the fare are copies of the impaired trace, which POL-RD-07(ii) excludes as circular. The driver's statement ('I took the KPE like always') denies a detour rather than conceding one, so it is not the route admission the clause names. The traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00110-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) is absent. POL-RD-10(3) therefore makes escalation mandatory, and POL-RD-10(1) requires it independently, because the fact the case turns on rests on a 0.39-weight artifact, below the 0.70 floor.

On the driver's remaining points: the $3.00 ERP is not refunded separately, because erp_gantries is null, the gantry match is undecidable on the record, the line is treated as matched, and no billing-integrity finding arises. No repeat-deviation pattern is established (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 744), so there is no POL-RD-06(b) uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. No pickup or dropoff amendment exists, so POL-RD-05 is unavailable. The driver's claim that he simply followed the platform's 'KPE then ECP' optimal corridor, and the rider's own '18-19 km' estimate, are both attempts to answer the one question the tunnel gap leaves open, and neither can answer it. The rider's enhanced-corroboration trigger under POL-RD-08 (deviation_claims_60d 1, substantiated 0) is not engaged.

Escalation is terminal: no refund and no driver payment issues, and the disputed $34.42 is held, not collected or refunded, pending human review. What would settle it: the fare's gantry itemisation showing which gantries were crossed, an untruncated chat covering the tunnel, or a trace that records the tunnel segment itself. No referral is issued, because no clause produces one on these facts.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
